title: A deep dive into the Peterverse
content:
The following is a reported look into a growing community on Instagram. To unlock more of my deep dives into emerging online spaces and internet trends, and to keep this newsletter alive, become a paid subscriber today. I cannot produce this newsletter without your financial support!

Subscribe now

Over the past couple months, thousands of Peter Griffin-themed accounts have cropped up on Instagram, espousing detailed information on everything from pop culture to religion, to niche political ideologies.

The sprawling network of pages have become known as the Peterverse, and they have amassed millions of collective followers and hundreds of millions of views. “There are even Peters who report on Peterverse news," one creator said.

Peter Griffin is one of the lead characters on the animated series Family Guy. Creators are using his image to produce AI generated educational videos. The trend began around the new year when someone created a Peter Griffin-themed account educating people on the Muslim religion. Copycats soon emerged.

Each account uses an image of Peter Griffin, sometimes customized to the account's theme (so goth Peter Griffin looks goth, for instance). In the videos, Peter breaks down a topic to another character (usually another character from Family Guy like Stewie or Meg), through an AI generated conversation using AI generated voice replication. The conversation happens over gaming footage, usually Minecraft gameplay.

queer.communist.peter
A post shared by @queer.communist.peter

Part of the reason the accounts are taking off is how easy they are to spin up thanks to the boom in AI tools. Apps like CapCut, Para AI and Character AI, allow users to create and publish a full video in less than 30 minutes.

While the videos might seem like your generic brain rot, there’s something deeper at play. I spoke to dozens of creators who run Peterverse pages and the young people who follow them. The accounts essentially function as a way for people— mostly teenagers— to find and connect with other kids over shared niche interests in a low pressure way. Nearly all the accounts are run by teenagers or young adults in their 20s.

Peterverse admins talked extensively about how lonely it is to be a young person these days. The accounts serve as discovery tools to find new people who they might have things in common with. "It's all teenagers, everyone in that young adult area, I don't think anyone in their 30s is running them," said Emma, a 21 year old who runs Trans Lesbian Peter Griffin.

Share

Nearly every Peter Griffin page admin I spoke to said that they wanted to find people to befriend and discuss things they’re interested in, but did not want to show their face online.

"I'm a person who gets nervous about taking a video of myself or talking with my face, said Will Zearfaus, 22, who runs a music-themed Peter Griffin account. "This [account] has let me talk about things I love but I don't have to use my voice or have people see my face.”

"When you're when you're using your face, you have to take different takes, make sure you're not laughing, smiling, there's the lighting, setting it up, tone, aesthetic," he added. "This is easy to set up. It cost me six bucks [for the AI software], it's a lot of fun to do."

fitnesspeterg
A post shared by @fitnesspeterg

At a time when most social interaction can feel superficial, Peter Griffin accounts allow the kids who primarily follow them to go deep on different topics and form tight bonds with others interested in the same things. Fans of different Peter Griffin accounts connect with others in group chats, Discord servers, and even Minecraft servers, to continue their discussions.

Many of the accounts provide incredibly valuable and thoughtful educational content on different topics. Kids I spoke to said that they'd learned a ton from the accounts and consider the format a good way to digest information because the conversational format and shortform structure makes it easy to learn about new topics. The gameplay footage in the background keeps you entertained while you’re learning.

petergriffinslovakia
A post shared by @petergriffinslovakia

"[The Peterverse] might be one of the few good little pieces of the internet, because they give some sort of educational content and because there's so many pages, it becomes hard for it to become an echo chamber of the same beliefs being spouted non stop," the teenage administrator of an anti-Scientology themed Peter Griffin account told me. "So [these accounts] subject young people to lots of different views, almost all at once."

Another teenager who runs a goth Peter Griffin page said that the communities the Peterverse has birthed feel deeply authentic because they're all faceless, so it's easier to speak freely and connect purely around shared topics of conversation.

Share

"A lot of people have texted me and DMed me and said I love your content can you talk about this or that, then we get into a conversation and talk about goth subjects," the teenager who runs Goth Peter Griffin, who asked to remain anonymous, said. "It's really cool. It's genuine."

Having the accounts all feature a well known character from TV also makes the pages feel familiar.

"You know this character Peter Griffin and you're familiar with him. He's a character that you can interpret anything into," an admin added. "When that character who you love is suddenly talking about your favorite interest, it's very appealing. I think so many young people are appreciating that other young people are expressing their thoughts. It's a good way to connect and also educate each other. It's given me a whole new perspective on the internet. I feel very appreciated."

comp.sci.peter
A post shared by @comp.sci.peter

Some members of the Peterverse have expanded into political activism, and have ventured into live streams, debates, and raising funds for things they care about. “I try and use my platform to raise mutual aid, it's been somewhat successful," said Age, the administrator of Maoist Peter Griffin.

While the vast majority of Peterverse accounts are wholesome and educational, there are some edgy teens who have made accounts espousing controversial views. “I've seen ISIS Peter Griffin or Nazi Peter Griffin," said Emma, the admin of Trans Lesbian Peter Griffin.

And since the accounts have gone viral, right wing internet trolls have attempted to leverage their popularity to spread far right messaging. “There's a nazi undercurrent that's been coming into the Peter scene," said Amos, a teenager who runs Emocore Peter Griffin. "When I say Nazis I mean literally Nazis. There's a national socialist Peter Griffin and Confederate Peter Griffin. A lot of alt-right culture dominates Meta sites like Instagram, and there's a strong undercurrent there."

comradpeter
A post shared by @comradpeter

As the format has gone mega viral marketers are already looking to tap in. Bruce, a 20 year old who asked to be referred to by his first name only, runs HAYAT media, an agency that helps accounts in the Peterverse monetize. Right now he's working with a slew of pages to help grow their revenue streams and run ads across their accounts.

"I run around seven Peter accounts and I have partnerships with more of them," he said. "There's Piracy Peter, Buddhist Peter, Kurdish Peter, Turkish Peter, we had one based on the Taliban. It's a big industry. We've got 121 Peters at this point. That's 121 creators making videos about different ideologies, different beliefs, different topics, all using this niche."

anti.zionist.peter
A post shared by @anti.zionist.peter

Bruce said that he helps the Peter accounts he works with generate scripts, edit the videos, and upload the content. He then sells ads to brands and gives the creators commission based on how many views they get. So far, several apps promoting AI tools and chat apps like one called Rizz, which helps optimize your text messages, have run ad campaigns across the Peterverse through Bruce's agency.

One thing Bruce said he won't let his Peter accounts do is crypto scams. "Imam Peter Griffin released a meme coin after he hit 50,000 followers, he promoted it and contacted other creators DMed them messages and said I'll give you this cut of the earnings we do," Bruce said. "But then he did a rug pull. He hasn't uploaded since."

Other accounts have begun brokering their own promotional deals within their niches.

"I started doing something that I don't think any other Peter did, which I started promoting bands on my account," the administrator of a hardcore music-themed Peter Griffin account told me. "I started off doing it for free but I was getting a lot of them, so what I did is put up a business venmo and I said if you want to skip the line you can send me $5. Right now I've made $100."

conspiracypeter
A post shared by @conspiracypeter

Luke, the 15 year old administrator of Magus Peter Griffin, a magic-themed Peter Griffin account, said that the Peterverse has boosted sales of his Amazon book about magic, and he's seen a 4,000% increase in streams to his music on Soundcloud thanks to the audience he's generated from the page.

"These accounts appeal to the younger mind that wants to pay attention to multiple things at once," he said. "The more you know about your niche, the better it is, because the knowledge just bleeds through."

The rise of the Peterverse on Instagram underscores a significant shift in online media where community-focused content is becoming the norm. More creators are also leveraging digital avatars to build their accounts, whether it's Peter Griffin or other characters from video games or nostalgic TV shows.

As the format evolves, Peterverse creators said they plan to try to expand the universe to include different popular characters.

"Once we're done with the Peterverse, we'll make one with the Simpsons in a similar pattern," Bruce said of his expansion plans. "We'll slowly integrate them together to grow the pages. Right now we are trying to do is collaborate with as many Peters as we can, we want to integrate all the Peters as well, maybe down the line we can make a specific platform around this."

Other creators are already burning out on the meme however, with some accounts quitting to focus on schoolwork or getting tired of making content. “People are already making junk accounts and spam Peters,” said one Peter Griffin account creator who asked to remain anonymous. “The meme can’t last forever.”

User Mag news rundown

  • Hasan Piker is back on Twitch after a one day suspension for comments about Rick Scott committing medicare fraud.

  • Bars are adding more food items to cocktails, like Swedish Fish, beef jerky, fried chicken and more.

  • Netflix’s live push continues with John Mulaney’s late-night talk show. Everybody’s Live with John Mulaney debuts on March 12th.﻿

  • A Facebook group for Cybertruck owners is full of videos of people flicking off Cybertrucks.

  • Four Loko is on a mission to capture the Gen Z market, partnering with creators and calling itself a “clean” beverage.

  • Ryanair is the first airline to end paper boarding passes.

  • Tradwife influencer Nara Smith has a smoothie at Erewhon now.

  • Comedian and influencer Hannah Berner interviewed Megan Thee Stallion on the Vanity Fair red carpet and caused a wave of controversy, opening up the age old debate of whether it was a good idea to replace red carpet journalists with influencers.

  • I live and die by (way too expensive but totally worth it) Mason Pearson hairbrushes and they’re becoming popular again thanks to TikTok.

  • Twenty years after it was founded, content discovery platform Digg is coming back, in a bid to “bring the fun back” to the internet.

  • Google’s AR beauty tool now lets you try on looks inspired by trends or celebrities.

  • Trump is charging $1M to attend candlelight dinners at Mar-a-Lago and if you want a one-on-one meeting, get ready to hand over $5M.

  • Your driving data goes to a half a dozen companies you’ve never even heard of for reasons you’d perhaps never agree to if asked directly.

  • The 2020 Gen Z TikTok star reunion tour continues.

  • ProPublica looked into science grants that Ted Cruz's team flagged as "radical" and "neo-Marxist" and here’s what they discovered:

    • Developing a device that could treat severe bleeding. It seems to have caught the committee’s attention for using the words “victims” — as in gunshot victims — and “trauma.”

    • Creating biosensors to detect infectious diseases. The grant appears to have been tagged for the repeated use of “POC,” an acronym often used for “people of color” but in this context meaning “point of care” — that is, the place where people receive medical treatment — and “barrier,” referring to a part of the biosensor itself.

    • Designing eye-tracking technology for diagnosing and treating concussions. It appears to have gotten flagged for referencing “traumatic” brain injuries and the “status,” meaning the condition, of patients.

  • Please let’s not make dark woke a thing.

  • An IG account that posts cute pics of wild animals like they’re celebrities.

  • Streaming has been a major setback for classic movies, largely due to platforms that ignore or bury old films— the oldest film on Netflix is from 1973 .

  • Scientists aiming to bring back the woolly mammoth create woolly mice (they’re very cute).

  • Interesting stat from : For the first time, Fox revealed that Fox Nation has about 2.5 million paid subscribers. That might sound impressive, Simon notes, but some simple math shows that the company has lost far more revenue to cable cord cutters than it gained from its subscription service.

    • Since 2014, cable has lost at least 30 million subscribers. Fox News generates an estimated $2 a month per subscriber. That means that it's lost somewhere around $720 million a year due to cord cutters.

  • Paloma Diamond, the fictional actor who’s become a phenomenon on TikTok, did a TMZ interview.

  • HBO’s The Last of Us might not be getting a third season.

  • Apple will no longer be selling Macs in the color space gray, replacing it with “space black.”

  • The dress Mikey Madison wore to the "Anora" film premiere was made up of hundreds of red, acrylic nails.

  • Elon Musk’s new haircut is something:
